summary: Dedicated throughput regression: autoscaler oscillation from delayed telemetry + background-checker evictions
description:
Issue summary:
NimbusAnalytics reported a sustained p99 latency and a 25-40% drop in dedicated throughput starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. The customer is on a Dedicated pool (dedicated-us-east-3) and runs long-context streaming workloads.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing increased inference latency (p99 up ~3-4x) and reduced completed throughput per GPU.
- Customer calls failing or falling back to lower-tier model variants during the window.
- Business impact: user-visible slowdowns for production features.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dedicated-us-east-3
- Customer tenant: nimbus-prod-1
- Models: gptx-3.8-8k-int8 (pinned by tenant)
- Observed between 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC and ongoing

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High-rate long-context streaming requests from tenant (steady-state for >30m).
2) Background health-checker sidecar (recent rollout) starts scanning model directories and triggers small prefetch/flushes on a subset of GPUs.
3) KV-cache growth from long-context sessions increases per-GPU memory pressure.
4) Autoscaler telemetry aggregation (60s window) delays visibility of memory/pipeline pressure.
5) Autoscaler scales down slightly in response to smoothed metrics, then rapid evictions / prefetch IO cause transient GPU unavailability.
6) Autoscaler then scales up; repeated cycles cause slot fragmentation and inefficient batching, producing throughput regression and p99 spikes.

Observed behavior:
- p50 stable; p99 jumps and sustained throughput decline.
- Frequent ephemeral evictions on 3-4 GPUs (logs show prefetch eviction + driver messages).
- Autoscaler activity correlated to metric smoothing window: scale decisions are always 30-90s behind the onset of noise.

Expected behavior:
- Stable throughput with predictable autoscaler decisions. Background maintenance jobs should not cause eviction on dedicated customer nodes. Autoscaler should not oscillate in response to short-lived IO noise.

Relevant logs & dashboards:
- Grafana: dashboard/dedicated/dedicated-us-east-3?var-tenant=nimbus-prod-1 (p99 latency and allocation churn)
- Kibana logs: /logs/prod/dedicated/evictions (attachment: eviction-trace-2026-03-10.log)
- Monitoring alert: AUTOSCALE-FLAP-ALARM fired 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC

Notes: customer provided request ids x-request-id: nimbus-req-3b2f. Support engineer captured a short session trace showing KV-cache growth to ~72% of per-GPU memory before first eviction.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC - Support (Aisha): initial triage, collected Grafana/Kibana links and requested sample request ids from customer.
2026-03-10 10:02 UTC - SRE (Marcus): observed autoscaler decision log timestamps delayed relative to eviction events; metric aggregation window confirmed at 60s for this pool.

2026-03-10 11:10 UTC - Eng (Elena Ramirez): identified a sidecar rollout (health-checker v1.2.4) that performs aggressive prefetch scans on `/models` every 20s; rollout targeted infra nodes but leaked into dedicated nodes via mislabeling.

2026-03-10 13:05 UTC - SRE: reproduced eviction pattern in staging by enabling health-checker on a test dedicated pool with long-context streams; observed autoscaler oscillation when aggregation window >30s.
2026-03-11 02:20 UTC - Hotfix applied: quarantined health-checker from dedicated node labels; increased min_replicas for dedicated-us-east-3 from 2 -> 4 to reduce shrink churn.
2026-03-11 03:00 UTC - Observed stabilization: p99 and throughput returned toward baseline after quarantine and min_replicas change.

2026-03-12 09:45 UTC - Engineering: proposal to reduce autoscaler aggregation window to 10s for dedicated pools with long-context customers and add heuristic to ignore short-lived eviction spikes when computing scale decisions.
2026-03-14 08:30 UTC - Follow-up: scheduled a config rollout and a permanent sidecar label fix; monitoring to continue for 72 hours post-rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Aisha (Support): Hi @NimbusAnalytics - thanks for the report. We see the p99 spikes on our side. We're investigating autoscaler activity and evictions; can you confirm whether your job spawns any background file operations?

2026-03-10 10:15 UTC - NimbusAnalytics (Customer): We don't run any explicit background jobs, but we did recently enable a debug mode in our client that might keep sessions open longer. Attaching request ids as requested.

2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - Marcus (SRE): We've found a health-checker sidecar rollout that ended up on dedicated nodes due to a mismatch in pod selector labels. Engineering is reverting the rollout from dedicated pools. Will update in 30m.

2026-03-11 03:10 UTC - Aisha (Support): Temporary mitigation applied (quarantine + min_replicas increase). Customer reports latency improvements. Keeping ticket open to validate stabilization and push permanent config fixes.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Elena Ramirez (Engineering): Creating follow-up PR to tighten label selectors for health-checker and add an autoscaler heuristic; linking PR in the ticket.
resolution: Partial mitigation deployed: health-checker sidecar quarantined off dedicated node label pool, min_replicas for dedicated-us-east-3 increased to 4 to prevent premature shrink. Observed throughput and p99 improved to within 10% of baseline. Full fix: engineering will roll out (1) label selector hardening for sidecars, (2) reduce autoscaler metric aggregation window to 10s for dedicated pools with long-context tenants, and (3) add eviction-spike ignore heuristic. Planned rollout scheduled 2026-03-15 with canary.
follow_up_actions: Engineering PRs: label selector fix (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1782) and autoscaler heuristic PR (TBD)
Runbook update: add guidance to isolate background maintenance jobs from dedicated customer nodes
Monitoring: add a dedicated probe to alert on eviction-frequency per GPU (threshold: >3 evictions / 15m)
Customer comms: schedule post-mortem and share root cause once PRs are merged
